News / Stock Story / What to expect from Dolby Laboratories’s Q3 earnings

What to expect from Dolby Laboratories’s Q3 earnings 1 min read

DLB

Audio and video technology company Dolby Laboratories DLB will be announcing earnings results this Tuesday after market close. Here’s what you need to know. Dolby Laboratories missed analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $305 million, down 3.3% year on year. It was a mixed quarter for the company, with revenue guidance for next quarter exceeding analysts’ expectations. Is Dolby Laboratories a buy or sell going into earnings? Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members . This quarter, the market is expecting Dolby Laboratories’s revenue to grow 20.9% year on year, improving from its flat revenue in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Dolby Laboratories has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years. Looking at Dolby Laboratories’s peers in the design software segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. Unity delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 32.2%, beating analysts’ expectations by 9.7%, and Procore Technologies reported revenues up 18.7%, topping estimates by 4.7%. Unity traded up 21.3% following the results while Procore Technologies was also up 19.7%. Read our full analysis of Unity’s results here and Procore Technologies’s results here . Investors in the design software segment have had steady hands going into earnings, with share prices flat over the last month. Dolby Laboratories is up 4.2% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $79 (compared to the current share price of $63.61). item.title: Bitcoin whales send $55M more to exchanges than they withdraw daily, Glassnode says
item.description: Bitcoin's largest holders are moving coins toward the trading desk. They have been doing it steadily for weeks.Whales are sending about $55 million more BTC to exchanges than they withdraw each day, ...
item.content:encoded:
News / Crypto Briefing / Bitcoin whales send $55M more to exchanges than they withdraw daily, Glassnode says

Bitcoin whales send $55M more to exchanges than they withdraw daily, Glassnode says 2 min read

BTCUSD Bitcoin's largest holders are moving coins toward the trading desk. They have been doing it steadily for weeks. Whales are sending about $55 million more BTC to exchanges than they withdraw each day, according to on-chain analytics firm Glassnode. The pattern signals rising sell pressure from the wallets with the most firepower in the market. Glassnode's report, dated November 15, 2026, focuses on whales: entities holding 1,000 BTC or more. The headline figure is a net number. Whales are depositing roughly $55 million more in BTC onto exchanges than they are pulling off each day. That surplus has persisted across several weeks rather than appearing as a one-day spike. To filter out daily noise, Glassnode looks at a 30-day moving average of whale net flows. That smoothed line shows persistent inflows to trading platforms. It also marks a change in direction. Earlier periods showed whales withdrawing more than they deposited, which typically suggests holding rather than selling. When the report landed, Bitcoin traded at approximately $64,853. That reflected a decline of about 1.16% on the day, amid broader weakness across the market. Glassnode categorizes the activity as positioning for potential distribution rather than immediate selling. The coins have been moved to the store shelf, but nobody has rung them up yet. A coin sitting in a long-term wallet is not easy to sell in a hurry. A coin sitting on an exchange can be sold with a few clicks. That is why watchers treat deposits from large holders as a supply signal. When whales consistently send more Bitcoin to exchanges than they take out, the pool of coins ready for sale grows. A bigger pool of ready supply can weigh on price if buyers do not show up to absorb it. Withdrawals work the other way. Coins leaving exchanges usually head into storage, which tightens available supply. Sustained withdrawals are often read as accumulation. None of this is a guarantee. A deposit can sit idle, serve as collateral, or move back out later. That is exactly why Glassnode frames the current behavior as preparation rather than a sell-off already in progress. Whale flows have swung hard in both directions in recent history. In August 2024, net deposits from whales peaked above 3,000 BTC per day. That surge later gave way to withdrawals as the market moved into recovery phases. By late 2024, the pendulum had swung fully. Net withdrawals exceeded 5,000 BTC per day during notable price rebounds, according to the historical data cited alongside Glassnode's findings. The price backdrop adds to the concern. Bitcoin's move toward the $60K to $63K range has been described as entering a "pain zone," a label tied to diminishing demand signals. With the asset trading near $64,853, that zone is not far below current levels. The signal worth watching is a reversal in the flows themselves. According to Glassnode's interpretation, a shift to sustained net withdrawals by whales could mark the end of the current distribution phase. If the 30-day average flips from inflows to outflows, it would suggest big holders are back to accumulating rather than preparing to sell. That flip has happened before. The move from heavy deposits in August 2024 to large withdrawals by late 2024 lined up with price rebounds.

item.description: Nvidia shares have fallen 32% from their October record high, as the Huang controversy compounds broader doubts about the durability of the AI boom. The company is scheduled to report quarterly ...
item.content:encoded:
News / CNBC TV18 /

Nvidia shares may bounce back as investors gauge Jensen Huang's comeback reports NVDA Nvidia Corp. shares may be poised for a rebound after the Financial Times reported that Jensen Huang is discussing a potential return to the chipmaker. Shares were little changed in early Robinhood trading after a perpetual futures contract on the Hyperliquid blockchain tied to Nvidia’s share price gained more than 3% on Sunday. Nasdaq 100 futures rose nearly 0.9% before reversing course and turning lower, a Bloomberg report said. Nvidia stock is coming off its worst week since April 2025, following Huang’s admission of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy and his swift departure from the company. The scandal at the technology bellwether has heightened concerns among investors already questioning how long the artificial intelligence boom can last. According to the Financial Times, Huang has been discussing a possible return, with support from several Silicon Valley allies. Altimeter Capital Management and Atreides Management are among those that have called on Nvidia’s board to reconsider, as has Tesla Inc. Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk. A website named Stand with Jensen has collected more than 164,000 names from people expressing support for Huang, including Nvidia employees and shareholders. An open letter posted on the site urges the board to reinstate him while an independent investigation is conducted. The likelihood of Huang’s return remains unclear. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is pressing the company to make a “dramatic” change in leadership and disclose whether it has complied with export controls on its prized AI chips. Nvidia shares have fallen 32% from their October record high, as the Huang controversy compounds broader doubts about the durability of the AI boom. The company is scheduled to report quarterly earnings on Tuesday, offering investors an update on the outlook for demand.

item.title: Nikkei, Kospi slide: Asian markets fall as Nvidia results, US inflation concerns keep investors cautious
item.description: Asian equities opened mostly lower on November 16, with Japanese and South Korean benchmarks sliding while Hong Kong futures pointed higher. The Nikkei 225 fell 0.99%, the Topix lost 0.17% and the ...
item.content:encoded:
News / CNBC TV18 /

Nikkei, Kospi slide: Asian markets fall as Nvidia results, US inflation concerns keep investors cautious NI225 KOSPI Asian equities opened mostly lower on November 16, with Japanese and South Korean benchmarks sliding while Hong Kong futures pointed higher. The Nikkei 225 fell 0.99%, the Topix lost 0.17% and the Kospi shed 0.33%. MSCI's gauge of Asian shares inched lower. Hang Seng futures rose 0.6%. In India, the GIFT Nifty which indicates how the country's market could open for the day's trade, pointed to a positive start. The MSCI India gauge has rebounded 11% from its October low, adding more than $400 billion in value and almost erasing this year's losses, as the country's limited AI exposure has become an advantage according to a Bloomberg report. The Japanese yen, meanwhile, was little changed at 159.67 per dollar and the offshore yuan at 6.6721. Data on Monday showed that Japan's economy contracted for the first time in a year as bad weather hit consumer spending. China's retail sales and industrial production figures are due. Wall Street futures pointed to a tentative recovery after a weak end to last week as Nasdaq 100 contracts gained 0.5% and S&P 500 futures added 0.2%, after both benchmarks closed lower for a second straight session on Friday. Dow Jones futures rose about 50 points, Nasdaq futures about 160 points, and S&P 500 futures nearly 20 points. On Friday the Dow recovered almost 350 points from its lows to finish just above the flat line. The Nasdaq ended 0.9% lower as pressure on Nvidia persisted, though it still posted its best week since August. Technology stocks drove the weakness as Nvidia capped its worst week since the April 2025 tariff selloff and lost more than half a trillion dollars in market value, while the Financial Times reported that ousted Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang was discussing a possible return to the company. The sector was also rattled by a Microsoft outage last week. Investors now seemed to await Nvidia's results on Tuesday and Anthropic's expected listing, which they seem to see as tests of appetite for the artificial intelligence trade, additionally, US retail sales and minutes of the Federal Reserve's latest meeting also loom. Inflation worries further seem to add to the caution as US producer prices rose 0.3% in October from September and 6.5% from a year earlier, the fastest annual pace in four years, though slightly below forecasts. Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said price pressures are running too hot, and policymakers have more work to do, citing energy costs, durable goods prices, the AI buildout and healthcare costs as per a Bloomberg report. Oil prices, meanwhile, steadied after a two-week slide. Brent traded at $96.29 a barrel, close to Friday's level, after losing more than 2% last week, while the US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) for December delivery barely moved at $88.46. Fresh attacks in West Asia revived concerns that the physical market may stay volatile. With Agency Inputs
